display.text: Summary of a model's ability to discriminate positive from negative cases across classification thresholds; larger values indicate better discrimination. Abbreviated AUC.
Model for a two-category response that expresses the log odds of the outcome coded 1 as a linear combination of predictors.
Proportion of observations whose predicted category agrees with the observed category at the chosen classification rule.
Table cross-classifying observed and predicted categories, showing correct and incorrect classifications.
Requirement that observations provide independent information in the standard logistic model; untreated repeated measurements can violate it.
Observation with a disproportionate impact on fitted model coefficients; influence and being unusual are related but distinct properties.
Test comparing the fit of a fuller logistic model with a nested simpler model; the example compares all predictors against an intercept-only model.
Weighted sum z = β₀ + β₁X₁ + … + βₖXₖ; in logistic regression it represents the modeled log odds.
Requirement that the specified predictor terms combine linearly to describe log odds, rather than requiring probability itself to change linearly.
Average negative log probability assigned to the observed binary outcomes: −Σ[y ln(p) + (1 − y)ln(1 − p)]/N. Confident incorrect predictions receive large penalties. Also called binary cross-entropy.
Change in the log odds of the modeled event for a one-unit predictor increase, holding other predictors fixed.
Natural logarithm of the event odds, ln[p/(1 − p)], modeled as a linear predictor in logistic regression. Also called log odds.
Logistic regression containing more than one predictor, with each coefficient interpreted conditional on the other predictors.
Baseline model with an intercept and no predictors, used for assessing improvement from a fuller logistic model.
Probability of an event divided by the probability of its absence: p/(1 − p). Odds are not the same as probability.
Multiplicative change in event odds for a one-unit predictor increase, holding other predictors fixed; OR = exp(β). Values above 1 increase odds, below 1 decrease them, and 1 leaves them unchanged.

Model-fit summaries for logistic regression, defined differently from ordinary least-squares R²; they should not be interpreted as ordinary proportions of outcome variance explained. Nagelkerke and McFadden are distinct versions of this measure.
Curve showing classification sensitivity against the false-positive rate as the decision threshold varies. Abbreviated ROC.
S-shaped function p = 1/(1 + e^(−z)) that converts a linear predictor z into a probability between 0 and 1. Also called the logistic function.
